papers.title: Suppression of heavy-ion fusion by slow quasifission
papers.authors: L. T. Bezzina, E. C. Simpson, D. J. Hinde, M. Dasgupta, J. Buete, K. Banerjee, A. C. Berriman, K. J. Cook, D. Y. Jeung, P. McGlynn, C. Simenel, and B. M. A. Swinton-Bland
papers.summary: Author(s): L. T. Bezzina, E. C. Simpson, D. J. Hinde, M. Dasgupta, J. Buete, K. Banerjee, A. C. Berriman, K. J. Cook, D. Y. Jeung, P. McGlynn, C. Simenel, and B. M. A. Swinton-BlandHeavy-element synthesis hinges on the formation of a compound nucleus — a fully equilibrated amalgam of the projectile and target nuclei — but quasifission, a fast reseparation process, can prevent this outcome. Using the SOLITAIRE separator to directly count evaporation residues from reactions forming 220Th, this work shows that fusion can be suppressed by more than 50% even when the classic fingerprint of quasifission — a correlation between fragment mass and emission angle — is completely absent. Instead, a subtle broadening of the fission mass distribution is observed that points to slow quasifssion as an explanation for the suppression - a feature whose significance becomes clear only alongside the evaporation residue measurements.[Phys. Rev. C 114, 054602] Published Thu Nov 05, 2026
